relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: A friendship between kings opens a corridor for timber, labor, food, and diplomacy.
Solomon turns his temple vision into a request to another nation.
David's wars are named as the reason sacred construction waited.
Peace arrives at the throne, but the meaning of rest will differ for workers.
Solomon claims the promised task of building a house for the Divine name.
He depends openly upon Sidonian expertise and offers negotiated wages to Hiram's workers.
Hiram celebrates wisdom that can sustain cooperation between peoples.
The cedar and cypress agreement is accepted.
Mountain trees will become sea rafts, while royal households exchange food for forest wealth.
Lebanon yields the materials Solomon desires.
Grain and oil flow yearly toward Hiram's house in return.
Wisdom appears as peace and covenant between kings.
Yet Solomon summons thirty thousand people into compulsory labor.
Rotations preserve some time at home but do not transform conscription into consent.
One hundred fifty thousand bodies carry and cut the foundation materials.
Thousands of supervisors turn human effort into a royal system.
Costly stones are drawn from earth to promise sacred permanence.
Israelite, Tyrian, and Gebalite workers prepare the house together, though royal names will dominate its memory.

contemplative_note: The temple begins as international cooperation and mass labor. Sacred beauty must remember the forest, the quarry, the backs beneath burdens, the months away from home, and the skilled foreigners whose work made the vision possible.
